prior_findings.evidence: controls.spec now asserts the .joy-base ring is centred under the thumb and that cash/hustle/nav boxes are identical before/after the drag and inside the viewport; passed in my run (25.7 s). e2e/__shots__/controls-after-joystick.png shows the ring drawn and the HUD in place.

Region-only tier-1 starters (businesses.ts:9-14) plus Red Mesa permits, Solenne port bonus and the Neon Vale medallion do change what you build: .eval/early.test.ts at 20 min gives Solenne 11 crate stalls, Red Mesa 8-14 fuel pumps, Neon Vale 17-20 repair stalls, Amberfield 17-18 egg stands, Verano 19-23 beach shacks, Ironhold 11-12 scrap forges. But the loop is still the same in every region: tap, then put the local stall on every small lot, then upgrade. The goal chain (data/progression.ts:69-85) is identical in all six regions, and the signature category is also the main rival's focus, which causes new finding #1.

src/core/pitch.ts builds every card number from the live constants and functions (demandMult, SEASON_MULT, TOURISM_*, HYPE_*, permitSeconds). Cards now read Logistics x1.14, Industry x1.28, hype x0.7-x1.5 (select.png, select-small.png). One leftover is listed as finding #9 (stale Free Port text in Politics.tsx:83).

projectIncome() uses the sim's lotIncome. Browser play: the card estimate equalled the post-purchase income in all 6 regions (Solenne 0.7/0.7, Red Mesa 0.9/0.9, Neon Vale 2.2/2.2, Amberfield 0.7/0.7, Verano 2.5/2.5, Ironhold 0.9/0.9; .eval/play2-390x844.json).

Rebuilds are now per chunk. world.spec [rebuild]: 1 lot -> 1/6-1/9 chunks in 11.5-27.0 ms vs 71-112 ms for the full city. Caveat: one upgrade tap with the squash animation rebuilds its chunk twice (World.ts:280,290).

(a) Each region now spawns at its own landmark (palazzo + campanile, adobe courthouse + water tower, glass civic tower, county hall + silo, domed assembly, clock-tower Diet). (b) Palms read as palms. (d/e) Blue-hour nights and per-floor neon in Neon Vale work. Still open: (c) the default follow camera is very tight, so a foreground roof or empty asphalt fills about 40 % of the first screen (world-solenne-day.png bottom third, world-amberfield-day.png, world-redmesa-day.png). Neon Vale 'day' is a near-black scene (world-neonvale-day.png). Amberfield's town ground is beige paving rather than the meadow #8fb35a the bible asks for. See finding #6.

NPC churn is now feed-only ('market'), rival toasts are throttled, toasts are held while a modal is open, and rank-up waits. But toasts still draw at top:212px (styles.css:279), over the lot-card header on 360x640 (.eval/shots2/360x640-redmesa-2-owned.png, where the card title and close button are hidden). While a sheet is open they move to the top and cover the cash card (ui-sheet-empire.png). See finding #4.
signWageDeal (actions.ts:274-285) charges wageDealCost, steps 0.1 up to a 0.3 ceiling, and at the ceiling erosion is still x0.58 (mechanics.ts:162). Strikes stay possible.

favour() (mechanics.ts:112) gives income tax x0.8/x1.2 and customs risk x0.8/x1.3 with the ruling party in every region, and Red Mesa permits x0.5/x1.5. The Politics sheet explains it. Minor: rm_nephew 'Refuse' still says 'Your next permit may take a while' (events.ts:140), but -15 alone never reaches the -25 threshold.
buyRivalLot (rivals.ts:238-243) removes the war once the rival has no same-category business left in that district. The new problem is that this remedy is usually unaffordable: finding #1.

tests/difficulty.test.ts orders the stars by purchasing-power net worth over 3 seeds with a 25 % margin (pp@30m: Amberfield $4.7-17.4M > Verano $6.0-8.5M > ... > Neon Vale), and Red Mesa was re-rated to 2 stars from that data.
Level-band growth (LEVEL_STAGES) and squash/grow solo meshes are in World.ts:261-290. ui.spec asserts b.pulsing(lot) is true after +1 and then returns to false, and it passed.

The controls test can now fail on the HUD bug. ui.spec still does the 'buy flow from the world' with b.give(5000) + b.teleport + b.session.select (ui.spec.ts:23-27), yet F15 evidence claims a 'walk-up buy'. The estimate check under the comment 'check it against what the business really earns' (ui.spec.ts:32-38) is only expect(est).toMatch(/≈ \$/). F16 is still passes:true on a 302 sign-in redirect (ASSUMED). F1 is still false. See finding #7.

Browser play, first 10 min: every event before 600 s was region-local in all 6 regions (e.g. Red Mesa rm_fuel, rm_reform, rm_gusher, rm_dust; Amberfield am_fair, am_locusts, am_parade, am_drought, am_coop). rival_offer is gated to >= 600 s and >= $4k x cost index. Sabotage now arrives at 621-672 s in 4/6 runs, which is acceptable.

findings: src/core/rivals.ts:104-124 (price war) + src/core/mechanics.ts:12 SIGNATURE_CATEGORY — expected: a new player opening the region's signature starter is not hit by an attack they cannot answer, and the toast's remedy ('Buy out their X business in D to end it') is something they can afford — observed: the signature category is exactly the big rival's focus (Solenne logistics/Vance, Red Mesa energy/Crane, Neon Vale tech/Quanta, Verano hospitality/Azure, Ironhold industry/Krauss), and price wars have no time or size gate (offers and sabotage wait 600 s; wars don't). With 3 starter stalls and events off, a −35 % war hit within 10 min in 42/48 runs, often within 10-60 s, and the buyout to end it cost $13K-$1.42B (Verano: $1.42B at 10 s). In my browser run, Solenne's first rival contact was 'Vance Maritime slashed prices… −35 % for 2 min' on a single $158 Crate Stall at about 3 min — how to reproduce: npx vitest run --config .eval/vitest.config.ts .eval/war.test.ts (prints first war time and buyout cost per seed); or node .eval/play2.mjs solenne and read toastsSeen.

src/core/state.ts:36-42 (initial rival lots) — expected: rivals start roughly at their designed size (RivalDef.startCash $250K-$40M, personalities as written) so the Rich List and the 'Acquire a rival' goal are a race you can join — observed: rivals are seeded on the best lots with tier-weighted businesses (weighted(..., x => x.tier)) at level 4-18, so some start with Resorts or Tech Startups worth billions. At t=0 (seed 21): Glasshouse $11.3B earning $4.15M/s, Vance Maritime $4.15B earning $5.33M/s, cautious 'Profitable. Boring.' Nimbus Labs $2.45B, while the 'We don't compete. We acquire.' mega-rival Quanta Dynamics is the smallest in Neon Vale at $46M. It is pure seed noise (seed 7: Azure $6.98B, Vance $3.09B). The player starts #20 of 20 and stays near the bottom of the Rich List for the whole M1 (ui-sheet-rivals.png: #1 $11.5B vs your $54K; the top rivals are 500-1000x the bot's 45-min net worth), and acquisition (1.5x their net worth) is out of reach for almost every rival within 45 min. Even the weakest rivals (Two Rivers $6.9M -> $15.3M, Fieldstone $2.1M -> $35M by 30 min) outgrow the bot player (30-min purchasing-power net worth $0.65M-$17M) — how to reproduce: npx vitest run --config .eval/vitest.config.ts .eval/rivals2.test.ts.

src/core/rivals.ts:37-52 (claimLot) — expected: rivals cannot spend money they don't have — observed: rivalAct checks only landPrice*reserve*3 < cash (rivals.ts:72), then claimLot also subtracts bizCost of a tier-weighted business without any check, so rivals go into debt (seed 21 at 15 min: Palmetto Holdings cash −$46.5M) and still get the asset. This compounds finding #2 — how to reproduce: .eval/rivals2.test.ts, look for 'cash=−'.

src/ui/styles.css:279 (.toasts top: 212px) + src/app/session.ts:350-355 — expected (T10b claim 'nothing over the lot card'): toasts never cover the lot card or the money readout — observed: on 360x640 the lot card starts at about y=235, and after a purchase the 'You opened…' and 'Goal complete…' toasts sit on the card header and hide the business name and close button (.eval/shots2/360x640-redmesa-2-owned.png). While any sheet is open the toasts move to top:8px and cover the cash card (e2e/__shots__/ui-sheet-empire.png, ui-sheet-politics.png, .eval/shots2/360x640-redmesa-5-empire.png). ui.spec only guards .rankup, not .toast, against the card — how to reproduce: node .eval/play2.mjs redmesa 360 640 and view the 2-owned and 5-empire shots.

src/ui/LotCard.tsx:84-104 (vacant lot list) — expected: on a phone, the first lot you tap shows the region's starter business up front — observed: a small vacant lot lists 11-13 businesses in catalog order (cart, kiosk, then the region starter, then tier-2s you can't afford), so the local starter is third. On 360x640 only about 2.5 entries fit in the card and the Fuel Pump starter is cut off below the fold (.eval/shots2/360x640-redmesa-1-vacant.png). On 390x844 it is the third card (.eval/shots2/390x844-redmesa-1-vacant.png). There is no 'recommended' or affordable-first ordering, so the region identity players are meant to feel in minute 1 is buried — how to reproduce: start Red Mesa on a 360x640 viewport, tap the nearest empty small lot.

src/world/camera.ts (follow framing) + src/world/themes.ts:102-117 (amberfield) and the neonvale theme vs docs/ART_BIBLE.md — expected: a 'sunlit diorama' first screen that sells each region — observed: the default follow camera still frames about 30-40 % of the portrait screen as empty asphalt or a single foreground roof (world-solenne-day.png bottom third, world-redmesa-day.png, world-amberfield-day.png, world-ironhold-day.png). The day shots look noticeably worse than the '-wide' views (dist 110, polar 0.9). Neon Vale 'day' is a near-black slab with a flat cyan plinth and an unlit glass box (world-neonvale-day.png). Amberfield's town ground renders as beige paving rather than meadow #8fb35a, so the 'golden plains' region reads as grey concrete (world-amberfield-wide.png) — how to reproduce: npm run build:test && npx playwright test e2e/world.spec.ts, then compare world-*-day.png with world-*-wide.png.

e2e/ui.spec.ts:22-38 + features.json F15/F16 — expected: evidence that matches the claims — observed: F15 evidence says 'walk-up buy of a cart', but the spec does b.give(5000), b.teleport(lot) and b.session.select(lot) (no tap, no walk, no Go there), and it builds a Fuel Pump, not a cart. The comment 'check it against what the business really earns' is followed only by expect(est).toMatch(/≈ \$/), which cannot fail on a wrong number (the unit test covers the maths, so the comment is misleading). F16 stays passes:true while its own evidence says the published link only answers a 302 to a sign-in gate (ASSUMED, not VERIFIED) — how to reproduce: read ui.spec.ts:22-38 and features.json F15/F16.

src/core/data/progression.ts:69-85 (goal chain) — expected (owner: the starting region changes what you do in the first 10-20 minutes): early goals that teach each region's signature (ship cargo in Solenne to boost the docks, beat a permit wait or expedite in Red Mesa, sign a wage deal before a strike in Ironhold, own 3 farms for the co-op in Amberfield, ride or skip the hype in Neon Vale, prepare for low season in Verano) — observed: all six regions get the identical generic chain (hustle 10 -> first business -> collect -> hustle upgrade -> level 5 -> own 3 -> manager -> bicycle -> ship cargo …), and the only signature hint is a HUD pill. With finding #5 (starter buried in the list), a new player meets the region's identity mostly as a multiplier — how to reproduce: start any two regions and compare the GOAL chip sequence.

src/ui/sheets/Politics.tsx:83 — expected: the Solenne Free Port panel describes the rules in force — observed: it still says 'Imports land tariff-free. Transship other regions' cargo through Solenne to pay 40 % of their import tariff'. It doesn't mention the export certificate (import tariff x0.5) or the +20 %/ship dock bonus that the region card and HUD advertise, and a Solenne-based player can't transship at all (trade.ts:42), yet the Trade sheet shows 'Transship via Solenne' as a selectable method from Solenne (.eval/shots2/390x844-solenne-5-trade.png) and only rejects it on the quote — how to reproduce: start Solenne, open Politics and Trade.

src/core/data/events.ts:140 (rm_nephew 'Refuse') — expected: the outcome text is true — observed: 'Your next permit may take a while' applies −15 Circle standing, but permits only slow at standing <= −25 (mechanics.ts:60-62, ENEMY_STANDING), so from a fresh 0 standing nothing changes — how to reproduce: newGame('redmesa'), resolve rm_nephew with Refuse, compare permitWait(s,'kiosk') before and after (identical).

src/core/actions.ts:75 — expected: correct English in player-facing toasts — observed: 'You opened a Egg Stand.' (Amberfield's starter, the first toast many players will see) — how to reproduce: start Amberfield and build an Egg Stand.
